items.title: Cyber chief: UK facing AI-powered attacks on critical infrastructure within two years
items.summary: The UK NCSC warns that AI-enabled attacks on critical national infrastructure are likely within two years, blaming underinvestment in IT and long-tolerated weaknesses now discoverable at scale.

items.title: 2026-018: Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory on two critical PHP flaws enabling unauthenticated remote code execution; fixes shipped in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, with PoCs already circulating.

items.title: 2026-019: Critical Vulnerability in GitLab Community and Enterprise Editions
items.summary: CERT-EU flags a critical GitLab CE/EE flaw allowing unauthenticated arbitrary code execution; patch internet-facing instances first and check for compromise.

items.title: 2026-017: Critical Vulnerability in Cisco Secure Email Gateway
items.summary: Critical Cisco Secure Email Gateway AMP flaw permits unauthenticated remote file write and root command execution; Cisco PSIRT confirms active exploitation, patch immediately.

items.title: Chinese hackers use ARTEX AI in automated attacks against 200 orgs
items.summary: Chinese threat actors reportedly used ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent AI pentesting framework, to automate attacks against 200+ organisations in 14 countries.

items.title: EU Commission to probe supermarket cyberattacks
items.summary: The European Commission will investigate the wave of supermarket cyberattacks; the Agriculture Commissioner said food security is not at risk but supply chain resilience is a concern.

items.title: Additional Ivanti Connect Secure zero-days exploited in the wild (CVE-2026-111357, CVE-2026-118527)
items.summary: Ivanti patched two more Connect Secure zero-days (CVE-2026-111357 privilege escalation, CVE-2026-118527 predictable identifiers); both are listed in CISA KEV as exploited.

items.title: Artificial intelligence and cyber intrusion
items.summary: NCSC assessment on AI-enabled intrusion trends with projections of the threat landscape to 2028, useful input for multi-year defensive planning.

items.title: AI coding agents are installing MCP servers that will never be patched
items.summary: Glow Labs research ('MCPhantom') found AI coding agents installing deprecated, never-to-be-patched MCP servers on developer machines in the majority of reviewed sessions.

items.title: Attackers Exploit Critical Siemens IoT2050 Flaw to Plant Remote Command Backdoors
items.summary: CVE-2026-58115 (CVSS 10.0), a missing-authentication flaw in Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices, is under active exploitation to plant remote command backdoors.

items.title: Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies
items.summary: Google and partners dismantled a botnet of over 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes shipped with preinstalled malware used for residential proxying and ad fraud, potentially cutting off 10M more devices.

items.title: UK cyber chief says the UK will face AI cyberattacks on critical infrastructure by 2028
items.summary: Wire coverage of the UK cyber chief's warning that AI-driven cyberattacks on critical infrastructure should be expected by 2028.

items.title: UK must expect AI-powered attack on critical infrastructure within two years, report says
items.summary: Reuters summary of the NCSC report urging UK organisations to prepare for an AI-powered attack on critical infrastructure within two years.

items.title: UK faces ‘unprecedented rise’ in cyberattacks in coming months, warns cyber chief
items.summary: The NCSC annual report warns of an 'unprecedented rise' in attacks, noting long-tolerated vulnerabilities can now be found and exploited at previously unimaginable scale.

items.title: Max-severity bug in widely used OT programming tool exploited to deliver Linux malware
items.summary: A maximum-severity bug in a widely used OT programming tool is being exploited to deploy Linux malware on industrial IoT gateways.

items.title: One Compromised Laptop, Billions Lost: The Binance Attack-Path Warning
items.summary: Analysis of the Binance theft highlighting how one compromised laptop plus weak system separation and untested attack paths escalated into systemic loss.

items.title: Google shuts down global botnet running on certified Android devices
items.summary: Google disrupted a botnet built on Videostrong-made certified Android devices shipped with pre-installed malware, which evaded security testing for years.

items.title: New cyberattack on supermarket fridges sweeps across Europe
items.summary: Reuters reports a new wave of cyberattacks against supermarket refrigeration systems spreading across Europe.

items.title: What exploited vulnerabilities have in common: A data-driven analysis of real-world attacks
items.summary: Microsoft data-driven analysis shows real-world exploitation concentrates in a small subset of CVEs, offering prioritisation criteria based on exploitation likelihood, exposure and blast radius.

items.title: Tageszusammenfassung - 02.11.2026
items.summary: CERT.at daily report notes supermarket refrigeration attacks spreading to Belgium, Luxembourg and Sweden after France, plus a Northflank security breach.

items.title: Rekordméretű kriptolopás a Binance-nél 2026. október 29-én mintegy 6,36 milliárd dollár értékű kriptoeszközt loptak el a Binance tárcáiból. A tíz blokkláncot érintő támadás legnagyobb része körülbelü…
items.summary: NKI reports roughly USD 6.36 billion in crypto assets stolen from Binance wallets on 29 October 2026, spanning ten blockchains in a record-sized theft.

items.title: North Korea denies being behind record $6.3bn Binance hack
items.summary: North Korea publicly denies responsibility for the record USD 6.3bn Binance hack that US agencies and analysts attribute to Pyongyang.

items.title: Attackers Target Unpatched CryptoPayment Gateway Flaw That Can Expose Wallet Credentials
items.summary: Attackers are targeting an unpatched CVSS 10.0 flaw (CVE-2026-81648) in the CryptoPayment Gateway WordPress plugin allowing arbitrary file deletion and credential exposure.

items.title: Fireperf: Open-source network testing tool for firewalls and routers
items.summary: IPFire released fireperf, an open-source tool to measure how firewalls and routers handle high connection-state rates, complementing bandwidth testers like iperf3.

items.title: US strikes Iran ahead of midterm elections
items.summary: US forces struck Qeshm Island in Iran, described by officials as limited and defensive, days before the midterms.

items.title: Russian bombing kills 26 people at Ukraine aid centre, Kyiv says
items.summary: Russian aerial bombing of a southern Ukrainian village killed 26 people at an aid centre, Kyiv says.

items.title: Unit 42 Threat Intelligence Highlights - Nov. 2, 2026
items.summary: Unit 42 threat intelligence roundup covering cyberespionage, financial extortion and rapid adoption of AI in offensive workflows.

items.title: Largest crypto exchange in Brazil confirms cyberattack as millions flow out of platform
items.summary: Brazil's largest crypto exchange Mercado Bitcoin confirmed a cyberattack, with blockchain analysts tracking more than USD 46 million leaving the platform.

items.title: Mistral CEO: Europe faces ‘complete trap’ without frontier AI
items.summary: Mistral's CEO warns Europe risks a 'complete trap' without its own frontier AI capability and calls for a European AI strategy.

items.title: AI Vulnerability Finding
items.summary: Schneier highlights a claim that 3% of all critical software security bugs ever recorded were found in the past month, driven by AI-assisted discovery.

items.title: Több ezer alkalmazott adatait lopták el a Belbiztonsági Minisztériumtól Az Egyesült Államok Belbiztonsági Minisztériumát (DHS) érintő korábbi adatszivárgás során több ezer alkalmazottjának személyes…
items.summary: Hungarian NKI reports that a prior breach at the US Department of Homeland Security exposed personal data of thousands of employees.

items.title: What human hackers still do better than AI, according to HackerOne’s CEO
items.summary: HackerOne's CEO argues humans still outperform AI on business-logic bugs and impact judgement, while AI-assisted submissions flood bounty programs.

items.title: I discovered a sound that leaks your exact location (and it's everywhere) - YouTube
items.summary: OSINT demonstration showing how faint aircraft noise in video audio can be matched via Doppler curves to ADS-B data to geolocate the recording.

items.title: California’s Bay Area debates data centres ahead of US midterm elections
items.summary: At least seven San Francisco Bay Area cities have passed data centre moratoriums ahead of US midterms, despite the region's AI industry role.

items.title: Poland’s court fight boils over
items.summary: Poland's rule-of-law dispute escalates as PM Tusk moves to undo judicial appointments made under the previous government.

items.title: Crisis over top court shapes Poland’s battle lines before 2027 election
items.summary: Poland's Constitutional Tribunal crisis is shaping political battle lines ahead of the 2027 election, with rival rule-of-law and coup narratives.

items.title: Why Europe shouldn’t celebrate a Democratic midterm victory
items.summary: Analysis arguing a Democratic midterm win would do little to constrain US foreign policy toward Europe.

items.title: Malaysia to hold meetings to prepare for rising cyber and geopolitical threats, PM says
items.summary: Malaysia's PM announced preparatory meetings to address rising cyber and geopolitical threats.

items.title: South Korea's Lee calls for powerful government-wide cybersecurity body
items.summary: South Korea's President Lee called for a powerful government-wide cybersecurity body.

items.title: Russia bombs aid center and shelter in southern Ukraine, killing 26, officials say
items.summary: Russian bombing of an aid centre and shelter in southern Ukraine killed 26 people, officials say.

items.title: Business groups mount fresh campaign for long-term renewal of information sharing law
items.summary: US business groups are pushing to attach a long-term renewal of the CISA 2015 information-sharing law to the annual defense authorization bill.

items.title: Trump raises doubts about renewed attacks on Iran
items.summary: President Trump cast doubt on further attacks against Iran following recent strikes.

items.title: Rewarding defenders with bigger bug bounties
items.summary: OpenAI is increasing security bug bounty payouts and adding report-quality, loyalty and priority campaign bonuses.

items.title: Preparing our next security sprint to harden OpenAI
items.summary: OpenAI announced an internal security sprint with Cathedral Systems to test and harden its defenses using AI.

items.title: Introducing the Grid Protectors Program
items.summary: OpenAI launched a Grid Protectors Program with utilities aimed at grid reliability and consumer electricity costs around compute campuses.

items.title: Hundreds of Mundane AI Apps Are Hiding Sexually Abusive Deepfake Features
items.summary: WIRED identified around 400 apps and sites tied to Chinese-language developers that hide sexually abusive deepfake generation features behind mundane AI tools.
